open_points.subject: A18 startup cleanup of unreferenced value bytes
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... are removed; nothing else is. A spool directory that cannot be removed does not stop the start
open_points.question: What happens when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be removed: does startup fail, or does the kernel start while leaving the file, and if it remains, may it ever be served or reused?
options: Refuse startup until the file can be removed
Start, leave it unserved, and retry removal at a later start
Start and allow later equal-byte writes to reuse it
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup, because only failed spool-directory removal is explicitly made non-fatal.

open_points.subject: A18 cleanup coverage for trial file fixtures
open_points.text: The data directory holds ... a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest ... On start, ... value bytes no record names ... are removed; nothing else is.
open_points.question: Does “value bytes no record names” include unreferenced file-fixture bytes published by a failed trial-case store call, or are such fixture bytes excluded and therefore retained by “nothing else is”?
options: Include both value-carriage bytes and trial file-fixture bytes
Include only value-carriage bytes and retain unreferenced file-fixture bytes
Store fixtures separately and define another cleanup rule for their unreferenced bytes
open_points.default_guess: Include every unreferenced content-addressed payload, including trial file fixtures, so a failed call cannot leave a file that K-10 does not permit the kernel to keep.
